title: The ranges ahead
hookLine: four more years: the Stoics in full, the great questions, the thinkers and the practices, and your own way

cards: The top of a hill has a trick it plays. You catch your breath, you look out, and you see that this wasn't the top of anything. Behind it, there's another ridge.
Behind that, a range. Blue, then paler blue, all the way to the edge of the sky. For some people that moment is deflating.
More climbing? For others it's the best part of the whole walk. The world is bigger than the hill.
Tomorrow, year one ends. Before the last look back down, today is for looking out.

teach.b: Year two: the porch. The Stoics in full. You met them in stories and practices; next year you read them properly, starting with Epictetus's handbook, in order, a line at a time.
The school took its name from the stoa, the painted porch in Athens where Zeno taught, so year two is named for it.
Year three: the great questions. Wisdom from every tradition, gathered by theme. What is a good life?
How do we face death? What do we owe each other? Each tradition answers in its own words, and each is heard without ranking, the way you listened this year as a guest.

teach.h: YEAR FOUR: THE THINKERS AND THE SCHOOLS.
teach.b: Year four: the thinkers and the schools. It opens with the Tao Te Ching, chapter by chapter, the old master's short, strange book, and goes on to the philosophers and the practices that grew around them.
Year five: the summit. Reading the sources yourself, walking with the poets, and finally, living your own way. By then, the path hands you less and asks more.
The questions you wrote yesterday will still be there. A few may have softened. Now the honest part.
Nobody knows how far you'll go. Some people walk the whole range. Some walk a year, and carry two practices for the rest of their lives, and that is a whole life's worth.
The ranges aren't a to-do list. They're there, the way mountains are there: to look at, to wonder at, and to walk when you're ready. One day at a time, like this one.

how: People on a long path of study often pause at the end of a year to look ahead at what comes next, without committing to all of it at once.

games.q: you reach the top of the hill and see more ridges behind it. what's your first move?
o: catch your breath and look out.
sprint for the farthest ridge right now.
games.why: the ranges are there to look at and wonder at first, and to walk one day at a time, when you're ready.

practice: Go to a window, or outside, and find the farthest thing you can see, a line of roofs, trees, hills, the sky's edge, and let your eyes rest there, soft and wide.
Then notice your breath, right here: the far thing and the near breath, both at once. Don't plan anything; just look out.

wordCard.voice: Stoa, the painted porch in Athens that names year two of the ranges ahead: the porch, the great questions, the thinkers, the summit. Today's word.
